\section{UMLS and OMOP/CDM crosswalk}
\label{sec:s-umls-omop}

\subsection{UMLS concept crosswalk (generated)}
\label{sec:s-umls-crosswalk}

This crosswalk maps each Genetic Evidence Model dimension and enumerated value to a Unified Medical Language System (UMLS) concept. It is produced by the mapping harness (\texttt{mapping/build\_umls\_crosswalk.py}), which resolves each term against the UMLS Metathesaurus through the UTS REST API; the machine-readable result is \texttt{mapping/umls\_crosswalk.yaml}. It is distinct from, and does not replace, the structural crosswalk in \Cref{sec:s-crosswalk}. Only concepts the harness actually resolved are reported as mapped; where the top automated match was not faithful, a curator either selected a faithful concept from the query's returned candidates (recorded in \texttt{mapping/adjudications.yaml}) or recorded that none was faithful. No concept identifier is asserted that a query did not return; entries with no faithful UMLS concept are reported as such rather than forced.

Each dimension \emph{axis} is mapped to a UMLS Semantic Type (which then constrains the search for that dimension's values, so axis and values are consistent by construction); each dimension \emph{value} is mapped to a Metathesaurus concept within that type.

\noindent\textbf{Coverage.} Of 88 GEM dimension entries, 39 are mapped (12 dimension axes to a semantic type; the rest to a concept, 28 by curator adjudication) and 38 have no faithful UMLS mapping---chiefly the ordinal credibility tiers, study-design ascertainment routes, and composite relational tokens, whose granularity the Metathesaurus does not represent. 11 remain flagged for review.

\subsection{OMOP CDM positioning (illustrative)}
\label{sec:s-omop-positioning}

The following worked examples position GEM dimensions relative to the OHDSI OMOP Common Data Model (CDM) and its standardised vocabularies. This is deliberately not a full crosswalk: it shows the partial alignment that exists and flags what the CDM does not natively capture for basic-science genetic evidence. OMOP CDM is built around observational patient-level clinical data (conditions, drugs, measurements, observations). GEM describes basic-science genetic evidence about gene-phenotype relationships, much of which has no patient-level home in the CDM. The examples below show the partial alignment that does exist and flag the gaps.

{\footnotesize
\begin{longtable}{@{}p{2.9cm} p{2.6cm} p{2.1cm} p{6.0cm}@{}}
\caption{Illustrative positioning of GEM dimensions against the OMOP CDM (hand-authored, not exhaustive).}\\
\toprule
GEM dimension & OMOP domain / table & Standard vocab. & Alignment and gap \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
GEM dimension & OMOP domain / table & Standard vocab. & Alignment and gap \\
\midrule
\endhead
phenotype\_scale (CLINICAL) & Condition\newline condition\_occurrence & SNOMED CT & A clinical-scale phenotype aligns with an OMOP Condition concept (SNOMED CT), the CDM's native representation of a clinical finding. \emph{Gap:} Molecular, cellular, histological and organismal phenotype scales have no Condition-domain representation; OMOP has no phenotype-scale axis. \\
\addlinespace
measurement\_target (EXPRESSION, ACTIVITY, ...) & Measurement\newline measurement & LOINC & A quantitative molecular readout is conceptually a Measurement; LOINC covers some assay readouts (e.g. enzyme activity panels). \emph{Gap:} Basic-science functional readouts (binding, localization, stability of a specific gene product in an experimental system) are rarely represented as standard LOINC Measurement concepts. \\
\addlinespace
target\_type (GENE) / resolution (GENE) & Observation / (Genomic CDM extension)\newline observation (or OMOP Genomic CDM) & HGNC (via the OMOP Genomic vocabulary effort) & A gene identity aligns with HGNC; the OHDSI Genomic CDM extension is the locus where gene- and variant-level data are being standardised. \emph{Gap:} The base OMOP CDM has no first-class gene or variant entity; this lives only in the evolving Genomic CDM extension, which is not yet a stable standard. \\
\addlinespace
organism & (none)\newline (none) & (none in CDM; NCBITaxon outside it) & No alignment. OMOP CDM is patient-centric (Homo sapiens implied) and has no concept of a model organism. \emph{Gap:} Model-organism evidence is entirely out of scope for the CDM; GEM's organism dimension maps to NCBITaxon (see the s15 crosswalk), not OMOP. \\
\addlinespace
method (GWAS, ASSOCIATION\_STUDY, ...) & (metadata / study-level, not CDM clinical domains)\newline (none; study design is not a CDM patient-data domain) & (none; partial coverage in MeSH/OBI outside OMOP) & No direct alignment. Study design / evidence-generation method is not a patient-level CDM domain. \emph{Gap:} The CDM records observations, not how upstream genetic evidence was generated; GEM's method hierarchy has no OMOP counterpart. \\
\addlinespace
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
